title: The week oil crossed $100: stocks fall for three days, the rupee tests 95.5 and the world's central banks turn hawkish
standfirst: So far this week the escalating US-Iran conflict has pushed Brent up nearly 12%, dragged the Nifty down about 1.7% and the rupee down 1%. The ECB hiked, the Fed and Bank of Japan look set to follow next week, and global bond yields hit multi-year highs. Friday's US CPI closes the week.

items.text: Three straight down sessions, including Wednesday's 813-point Sensex fall to a three-month low, before a closing-auction rebound on Thursday. Broader markets have underperformed the large caps.
The rupee has lost about 1% this week to 95.46 per dollar; the RBI is selling dollars through state banks but appears content to let the currency adjust gradually.
The RBI shifted decisively to draining liquidity: currency swaps to mop up a $115 billion surplus and a ₹5 lakh crore 26-day reverse repo auction on Friday.
Regulators used the Global Fintech Fest to launch Demat 2.0 tokenised bonds, flag data and cyber obligations for fintechs, and float inflation-linked bonds for pensions.
SEBI conceded the new Closing Auction Session is amplifying expiry-day swings and will rework derivatives settlement pricing; the mechanism itself stays.
Brent crude rose from the low $90s to above $105 as US-Iran strikes escalated, the first time above $100 since late July. Energy is now the main driver of inflation expectations everywhere.

The ECB raised its deposit rate to 2.50% and signalled more; US producer prices ran hot and Fed funds futures moved to a 70% chance of a hike on 16 September; the Bank of Japan is expected to tighten too.
Global bond yields hit multi-year highs, with the US 10-year near 5% and a European sell-off deepening after the ECB's inflation warning.
Wall Street fell for three sessions; chip and AI names led the declines as the rally in semiconductors paused. Bitcoin drifted toward $77,000.
The US-Canada trade war escalated with new US import bans, while the IMF reportedly dropped its top choice for chief economist over his criticism of US tariffs.

watch: Friday 11 Sep: US August CPI; RBI's 26-day VRRR auction; Indian markets react to a third weak Wall Street close.
Early next week: India's August CPI (Reuters poll: 20-month high) and WPI.
16 September: Federal Reserve decision, followed by the Bank of Japan.
Brent's path above $105 and whether the rupee breaks 96 per dollar.
